learn.hook: What if a river could talk to you? What advice would it give?
points: The lesson 'The Day the River Spoke' is about a girl, a river and her wish to learn. Here we read our own short story on the same idea.
Every story has characters (who), a setting (where and when) and a plot (what happens).
The theme is the big idea or message of a story, such as courage or the right to learn.
Personification gives human actions to non-living things: 'The river whispered a secret.'
Clues in the text help us infer feelings: a girl who whispers her wish may feel shy or unsure.

example.q: Read: Every morning, Meera sat on the steps by the river and watched children walk to school with their bags. "I want to read books too," she whispered. The river splashed softly and said, "Go on, little one. Even I keep moving forward." The next day, Meera asked her father if she could join the village school. How does Meera feel at first, and what helps her act?
steps: Find the clue: she 'whispered' her wish, so she feels shy but longs to study.
Notice what changes: the river tells her to keep moving forward.
See the result: the next day she asks her father about school.
example.answer: At first Meera longs to study but is shy; the river's words give her courage, so she asks her father to let her join school.

learn.reallife: When you look at a river, a tree or the moon and imagine it talking, you are using personification, just like poets and storytellers do.

games.title: Story sequence
items: Meera watches children walk to school.
She whispers her wish to read books.
The river tells her to keep moving forward.
Meera asks her father if she can join school.

games.title: Story elements
items: The setting tells where and when a story happens.
Setting = place and time of the story.
Personification compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.
That is a simile. Personification gives human qualities to things.
The plot is the chain of events in a story.
Plot is what happens, from beginning to end.
'The wind whistled a happy tune' is an example of personification.
Wind cannot really whistle a tune; it is given a human action.
The theme of a story is the same thing as its title.
The title is the name; the theme is the big idea or message.

quiz.q: 'Every morning, Meera sat on the steps by the river and watched children walk to school.' What is the setting of this line?
options: The steps by a river, in the morning
A busy market in the evening
quiz.explain: The line says Meera sat 'on the steps by the river' 'every morning' — that is the place and time.
steps: The setting of a story is where and when it happens.
The line gives the place: 'on the steps by the river', and the time: 'every morning'.
So the setting is the steps by a river, in the morning.
Answer: The steps by a river, in the morning
quiz.mistake: Confuses the place the other children are going to with the place where Meera is

quiz.q: '"I want to read books too," Meera whispered.' What does Meera wish for?
options: To buy a new school bag
To study and read like the other children
To stay at home all day
quiz.explain: She says she wants to read books 'too', like the children going to school.
steps: Meera says, 'I want to read books too.'
'Too' means like the children she watches going to school.
So she wishes to study and read like the other children.
Answer: To study and read like the other children
quiz.mistake: Picks a detail (the bags) instead of what she actually says

quiz.q: 'The river splashed softly and said, "Go on, little one."' Which figure of speech is used here?
quiz.explain: A river cannot speak, so giving it speech is personification.
steps: A river cannot really speak.
Giving a non-living thing a human action (speaking) is personification.
There is no repeated sound (alliteration) and no 'like/as' (simile).
So the figure of speech is personification.
Answer: Personification
quiz.mistake: Thinks any imaginative line is a simile, even without 'like' or 'as'

quiz.q: Which sentence uses personification?
options: The river sang a soft song to the girl.
The river was cold and clear.
The river is near the village.
quiz.explain: Only a person can sing a song; giving this action to a river is personification.
steps: Personification gives human actions to non-living things.
Only a person can sing a song, so 'The river sang a soft song' gives the river a human action.
The other sentences just describe the river or Meera.
So the answer is 'The river sang a soft song to the girl.'
Answer: The river sang a soft song to the girl.
quiz.mistake: Thinks describing a thing with adjectives is personification

quiz.q: 'Meera whispered her wish so that no one could hear.' This most likely shows that she feels:
quiz.explain: Whispering so no one hears suggests she is shy or not sure anyone will listen.
steps: Clue: she whispers 'so that no one could hear'.
People speak softly like this when they feel shy or are not sure anyone will listen.
She is not loud, bored or boastful.
So she feels shy and unsure.
Answer: shy and unsure
quiz.mistake: Does not use the clue word 'whispered' to infer the feeling

quiz.q: What is the theme of a story?
options: The number of pages in it
The name of the main character
The place where it was printed
The big idea or message the story shares
quiz.explain: The theme is the central idea, like 'every child deserves to learn'.
steps: The theme is the big idea or message of a story, such as courage.
It is not the page count, a character's name or the printing place.
So the theme is the big idea or message the story shares.
Answer: The big idea or message the story shares
quiz.mistake: Mixes up theme with other facts about a book

quiz.q: '"Even I keep moving forward," said the river.' What lesson does the river give Meera?
options: Keep going and don't stop trying
quiz.explain: A river always flows on; it tells Meera to keep moving towards her goal.
steps: A river always keeps flowing forward.
By saying 'Even I keep moving forward', it tells Meera to do the same.
So the lesson is: keep going and don't stop trying.
Answer: Keep going and don't stop trying
quiz.mistake: Reads the line literally instead of as advice

quiz.q: 'The next day, Meera asked her father if she could join the village school.' This shows that Meera:
options: found the courage to act on her wish
quiz.explain: She moves from only wishing to actually asking — that takes courage.
steps: Before, Meera only whispered her wish.
Now she actually asks her father to let her join school.
Moving from wishing to acting shows she found the courage to act on her wish.
Answer: found the courage to act on her wish
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the ending with how the character has changed

teach.ask: Tweet! Gappu saw a story where a river talks! Can rivers really talk? What do we call it when a writer makes a river act like a person?
teach.praise: Wow! So when I say 'the sun smiled', I'm using personification too!
teach.nudge: But what kind of things get human actions in personification?

revise.summary: This story is about Meera, who longs to go to school; the river's words give her courage to ask. Stories have characters, a setting and a plot, a theme, and may use personification.
focus: Identify the characters, setting and plot of a short story
Find the theme (the big idea or message)
Spot personification and infer feelings from clues
remember: Setting = where and when; plot = what happens
Theme = the big idea or message of a story
Personification = giving human actions to non-living things, e.g. 'The river whispered a secret.'
traps: Don't confuse the theme with the main character's name
A talking river is personification, not a simile
Infer feelings from clues like whispering, not from guesses

learn.hook: In 1848, Savitribai Phule and Jyotirao Phule started a school for girls in Pune, when very few girls in India went to school.
points: Education means learning and growing by reading, thinking and asking questions.
When girls study, they can follow their dreams, earn a living and help their families and villages.
India's Right to Education Act (2009) gives every child aged 6 to 14 the right to free and compulsory schooling.
Word family: educate (verb), education (noun), educated (adjective), educator (a person who teaches).
Literate means able to read and write; its opposite is illiterate.

example.q: Read: Ritu's grandmother never went to school. Now Ritu teaches her the letters on bus boards, and Nani proudly reads out the name of their town. What does this show?
steps: Ritu learned at school.
She shares her learning with her grandmother.
Nani learns to read even when she is old.
example.answer: Learning can happen at any age, and an educated girl can spread her learning to her whole family.

learn.reallife: Look around: girls and women work as doctors, pilots, scientists, teachers and police officers — education opened those doors.

games.title: Words about learning
pairs: a strong wish to achieve something
money given to help a student study

quiz.q: Which word means 'able to read and write'?
quiz.explain: Literate means able to read and write. Literature means books and writing; literal means exact.
steps: 'Literate' means able to read and write.
'Literature' means books and writing; 'literal' means exact; 'illiterate' is the opposite.
So the answer is 'literate'.
Answer: literate
quiz.mistake: Confuses words that look alike

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'literate'?
quiz.explain: The prefix il- is used before words starting with l: literate → illiterate.
steps: Before words beginning with 'l', the negative prefix is 'il-'.
literate → illiterate.
'inliterate', 'disliterate' and 'unliterate' are not English words.
So the opposite is 'illiterate'.
Answer: illiterate
quiz.mistake: Uses the common prefix un- or dis- without checking the correct form

quiz.q: India's Right to Education Act gives free and compulsory schooling to children aged:
quiz.explain: The Right to Education Act, 2009 covers children from 6 to 14 years of age.
steps: The Right to Education Act was passed in 2009.
It gives free and compulsory schooling to every child aged 6 to 14.
So the answer is 6 to 14 years.
Answer: 6 to 14 years
quiz.mistake: Guesses a familiar school-age range instead of the one in the law

quiz.q: Who, along with Jyotirao Phule, started a school for girls in Pune in 1848?
quiz.explain: Savitribai Phule taught at the girls' school she and Jyotirao Phule started in Pune in 1848.
steps: In 1848 a school for girls was started in Pune.
Savitribai Phule started it with Jyotirao Phule and taught there.
So the answer is Savitribai Phule.
Answer: Savitribai Phule
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous Indian woman without matching her work

quiz.q: Which word in this family is a noun: educate, education, educated, educational?
quiz.explain: 'Education' names a thing (the process of learning). 'Educate' is a verb; 'educated' and 'educational' are adjectives.
steps: A noun names a person, place, thing or idea.
'Education' names the process of learning.
'Educate' is a verb; 'educated' and 'educational' are adjectives.
So the noun is 'education'.
Answer: education
quiz.mistake: Does not notice how endings like -ion, -ed and -al change the word class

quiz.q: Choose the right word: 'My aunt is an ___ woman; she has a college degree.'
quiz.explain: An adjective is needed to describe 'woman', so 'educated' fits.
steps: The blank describes the noun 'woman', so we need an adjective.
'Educated' is the adjective: 'an educated woman'.
'Educate' is a verb and 'education' is a noun.
So the answer is 'educated'.
Answer: educated
quiz.mistake: Uses the verb or noun form where an adjective is needed

quiz.q: 'Ritu teaches her grandmother to read the names on bus boards.' What does this tell us?
options: People can learn at any age
Bus boards are hard to find
Ritu does not go to school
quiz.explain: Nani is learning to read in her old age, so learning has no age limit.
steps: Ritu's grandmother is old, yet she is learning to read bus boards.
This shows learning has no age limit.
So it tells us people can learn at any age.
Answer: People can learn at any age
quiz.mistake: Adds an idea that is not in the text

quiz.q: Which sentence BEST matches the idea of 'education for all'?
options: School is only for children in cities.
Only boys need to go to school.
Every child, girl or boy, should get the chance to learn.
quiz.explain: 'For all' means everyone — every girl and every boy, in villages and cities.
steps: 'For all' means for everyone.
Only one sentence includes every child, girl or boy.
The others leave out girls or village children.
So the answer is 'Every child, girl or boy, should get the chance to learn.'
Answer: Every child, girl or boy, should get the chance to learn.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand that 'all' includes everyone

teach.ask: Gappu asks: why should girls go to school just like boys?
teach.praise: Yes! Every chick in the nest deserves to learn to fly — girls and boys!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what education helps girls do in their future?

revise.summary: Education means learning by reading, thinking and asking questions. When girls study they can follow their dreams and help their families, and India's Right to Education Act gives every child aged 6 to 14 free schooling.
focus: Know the meaning of literate, illiterate and the education word family
Know the Right to Education Act and its age group
Explain why education for girls matters, with examples
remember: Right to Education Act (2009): free and compulsory schooling for children aged 6 to 14
Literate = able to read and write; opposite: illiterate
Savitribai and Jyotirao Phule started a girls' school in Pune in 1848
traps: Don't confuse literate with literal or literature
The opposite of literate is illiterate, not unliterate
'Educated' describes a person; 'education' is the noun

learn.hook: The words river, Narmada, flock and hope are all nouns — but each is a different kind!
points: A noun is a naming word for a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
Common noun: a general name — girl, river, school.
Proper noun: a special name that begins with a capital letter — Meera, Narmada, Pune, Diwali.
Collective noun: a name for a group — a flock of birds, a herd of cows, a bunch of keys.
Abstract noun: a quality, feeling or idea you cannot touch — courage, honesty, knowledge, friendship.

example.q: Find the nouns and their kinds: 'A class of girls showed great courage on the banks of the Ganga.'
steps: 'class' names a group → collective noun
'girls' and 'banks' are general names → common nouns
'courage' is a quality we cannot touch → abstract noun
'Ganga' is a special name with a capital letter → proper noun
example.answer: class (collective), girls and banks (common), courage (abstract), Ganga (proper)

learn.reallife: Shop signs, maps and your school ID card are full of proper nouns — that's why they begin with capital letters.

games.title: Sort the nouns
items: river
teacher
book
Narmada
Diwali
Mumbai
courage
friendship
honesty

quiz.q: Which of these is a proper noun?
quiz.explain: Kaveri is the special name of one river, so it is a proper noun and starts with a capital letter.
steps: A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing and starts with a capital.
'Kaveri' is the name of one particular river.
'village', 'river' and 'school' are general (common) nouns.
So the proper noun is 'Kaveri'.
Answer: Kaveri
quiz.mistake: Thinks any place word is a proper noun

quiz.q: Which of these is an abstract noun?
quiz.explain: Honesty is a quality — you cannot see or touch it. The others are things or people.
steps: An abstract noun is a quality, feeling or idea that we cannot touch.
Honesty is a quality.
Garden, pencil and teacher can be seen or touched.
So the abstract noun is 'honesty'.
Answer: honesty
quiz.mistake: Does not know that abstract nouns name qualities and feelings

quiz.q: 'A herd of elephants crossed the river.' Which word is the collective noun?
quiz.explain: 'Herd' is the name for a group of elephants.
steps: A collective noun names a group.
'Herd' is the name for a group of elephants.
'Elephants' and 'river' are common nouns; 'crossed' is a verb.
So the collective noun is 'herd'.
Answer: herd
quiz.mistake: Picks the animals instead of the word naming their group

quiz.q: Complete: 'a ___ of fish'
quiz.explain: A group of fish swimming together is called a school (or shoal).
steps: A group of fish swimming together is called a school (or shoal).
Herd is for cattle, flock for birds or sheep, pride for lions.
So the answer is 'school'.
Answer: school
quiz.mistake: Uses a group word that belongs to other animals

quiz.q: Which words need capital letters in: 'meera visited jaipur in december.'?
quiz.explain: The first word of a sentence and proper nouns (a name, a city, a month) begin with capital letters.
steps: The first word of a sentence takes a capital: 'Meera' (also a name).
Proper nouns take capitals: 'Jaipur' (a city), 'December' (a month).
'visited' and 'in' are ordinary words.
So Meera, Jaipur, December need capitals.
Answer: Meera, Jaipur, December
quiz.mistake: Forgets that names of places and months are proper nouns

quiz.q: 'Her kindness made everyone smile.' The word 'kindness' is:
quiz.explain: Kindness is a quality we feel but cannot touch, so it is an abstract noun.
steps: Kindness is a quality we can feel but cannot touch.
Such a noun is an abstract noun.
It is not a name (proper), a group (collective) or an action (verb).
So 'kindness' is an abstract noun.
Answer: an abstract noun
quiz.mistake: Thinks only things you can touch can be nouns

quiz.q: What is the noun form of 'brave'?
quiz.explain: 'Bravery' names the quality. 'Bravely' is an adverb; 'braver' and 'bravest' are adjectives.
steps: We need the noun that names the quality of being brave.
'Bravely' is an adverb; 'braver' and 'bravest' are adjectives.
'Bravery' is the noun.
So the answer is 'bravery'.
Answer: bravery
quiz.mistake: Confuses the noun with other forms of the word

quiz.q: Complete: 'a ___ of wolves'
quiz.explain: A group of wolves is called a pack.
steps: A group of wolves is called a pack.
A swarm is for bees, a bunch for keys or grapes, a library for books.
So the answer is 'pack'.
Answer: pack
quiz.mistake: Mixes up collective nouns for different animals

teach.ask: Gappu found the words 'Meera', 'river' and 'courage'. Are they all the same kind of noun? Explain to him.
teach.praise: Chirp! Meera is proper, river is common and courage is abstract. Got it!
teach.nudge: Hmm, what kind of noun is 'courage' — something you can touch?

revise.summary: A noun is a naming word. Common nouns are general names, proper nouns are special names with capitals, collective nouns name groups, and abstract nouns name qualities, feelings or ideas.
focus: Sort nouns into common, proper, collective and abstract
Use the correct collective noun for a group
Form abstract nouns from adjectives and use capital letters for proper nouns
remember: Proper nouns begin with a capital letter: Meera, Kaveri, Pune, December
Collective nouns: a herd of elephants, a flock of birds, a school of fish, a pack of wolves
Abstract nouns: courage, honesty, kindness, bravery
traps: Don't write proper nouns like city or month names with small letters
Bravely is an adverb; the noun is bravery
The collective noun is the group word (herd), not the animals
